posts.cooked:
Not a snappy title, but it should make the potential spoilerificness of the thread obvious. Just in case it isn't enough though

 

Spoilers of Villains cards Ahead. Also, Massive Wall of Text

 

First off, let's talk oversized cards.

 

They are absolutely gorgeous. The artwork is superb and a few of them are, IMO, far superior in giving the feel of the villain than the original art. Bravo to Adam.

 

However, while ogling the art I noticed a few things, as I tend to do.

 

Base omnitron while in his factory form is shown expelling a lot of toxic green goo. I don't know if this ends up meaning anything, but It was not something I expected to see. I makes me wonder how environmentall unfriendly omnitron was.

 

Operative's flip doesn't give any clues to where those arrows came from, but showing the sign of Zhu Long so prominently gets me wondering. After all, after her near death she was sent to Zhu Long, and we still don't know how he and Chairman are connected.

 

Apostates flip makes the blue scars he had more interesting. They are spouting blue flame, which means it is energy leaking from within him. It is also breaking up the ground at his feet and makes me wonder about his title as a "corrupter"

 

I can't remember if this was ever brought up before, but La Capitan's flip  showing her split across time made me realize something. If I am not mistaken she has Atum's Gauntlet in one picture and the Starshield Necklace in another. Looking at the Starshield pic, she looks more like a ragged pirate, and I wonder if she appeared in Maine. The flavor text of the Starshield says it is a charm against evil from dreams. That, combined with all the other references, sounds like cthulu and if memory serves me, part of Lovecraft's universe involved pirates in Maine running into the "Deep Ones" which were monster fish people back in 1800's. She could have been there.

 

Here's a big one. Tormented Ally Infinitor. First of all, sounds like an awesome concept for him, but his flip side suddenly struck me with a few facts. His cards are manisfestations, not illusions or distortions or anything else. Something is manifesting through him, and his flip is "Overcome by Manisfestations" and shows a rather large sort of demonic horned being. At first I thought this might be our first visual of the Cosmic Entity, but looking over Infinitor's backstory he did supposedly draw from some being's power. I think this thing is the source of Infinitor's strength and insanity, but what it actually is I have no idea.

 

Looking toward the variants.

 

Chrono-Ranger's Best of Times promo, incapped, I think this is clearly the origin of Renegade (http://greaterthangames.com/content/for-profit-characters). My question is whose giant blast of green death is it that ripped him apart like that. I can't think of anyone except Gloomweaver who generally uses green blasts... oh, except Infinitor, that's a good potential canidate.

 

Adamant Writhe's incap side shows the "black wire being" again, but clearly seperated from Writhe. What is more interesting to me though is where thye are at. It looks to be the same place where Medico's incap is, note the giant blue-black vortex, it also looks the exact same as the scene we see in Deadline's Pandemonium Key and potentially where Chrono-Ranger ended up before Old La Capitan finds him. I'm wondering if this is one of the final arena's of the game.

 

Chokepoint had a few interesting bits.

 

Stripped Resources: It looks like Unity repaired O-X while they were fighitng Chokepoint

Material Upheaval: Looks like Chokepoint breaks into Fort Adamant

Empowered Self-Repair: She's talking to Swift bot, saying " Pushed into limbed form, but that is not your truth" gives some insight into Choke's mentality

Harvest the mighty: She's ripping apart the bunker suit. Considering she focuses on metal that would explain why bunker ends up fighting in the synth and tree suit.

Newfound Power: This looks like her recoery/transformation from Deadline's tool. she says, "I don't understand. You're so loud! So Bright!". I'm beginning to suspect that the blue stone is one of the Oblivion Shards, that would explain why it so drastically changed her capabilites.

 

A tangent of that led me back to the Dreamer, I'm thinking the green crystal the dreamer is often seen with is also an Oblivion shard. I think we've suspected that since we saw Man-grove's transformation in Tactics, but I think there may be more to it. The Visionary's mother was killed by the drugs that Project Cocoon used to give Visionary her powers. However, The Dreamer's mother is still perfectly healthy from everything we can see. Visionary had powers by two months, Dreamer got them by age six years. Even if we accept Vanessa Long will develop powers regardless of anything else, that is too much of a difference. What if contact with the crystal was the source of her power? What if that is what awakened her. And if we look, she has the crystal with the stuffed monkey. The Treacherous ape has the crystal, and the alternate version of dreamer we see in La Capitan's deck is accompanied by a large orange monkey, with a glowing gen in it's forhead. That is too much for coincendences.

 

Celestial Tribunal.

 

First off, we see The Matriarch being tried by the Tribunal, and the Dark Watch team is called in to testify in her case. I'm willing to bet this trial is the turning point that leads the Matriarch to become Pinion.

 

Looks like Heartbreaker killed Dr. Tremata. Also a guy with glasses and a faceless man, neither of whom I can identify. Looking at Heartbreaker's card later on (Miss info's deck) he's a nemesis of the entire Dark Watch team, and with the body's seen at the Tribunal I get the feeling he is a hired hitman, an assassin who Dark Watch has been hunting for sometime. I'm still wondering if he is actually Tony Taurus, but I don't think we'll learn that information until For Profit comes out.

 

The Star Field in the background of the Tribunal looks very similiar to me to the star fields mentioned above with Adamant and the Pandemonium key. If they are, that places it according to the Tribunal's card, at the edge of the Solar System.

 

Paragon of Sentience makes mention of the "Zenith of Humanity" while showing a picture of scholar and Guise fighting Aeon Men. That could mean scholar, which makes a lot of sense I think, or guise, which makes less immediate sense but then sort of makes sense considering all Guise does seems to be ripping off pop references while being a hero. I'll also come back to this card later.

 

Court of Blood, oh man, I get the feeling I'm going to love to hate this environment.

 

One really cool but subtle thing is that the Blood Countess is shown wearing cross-shaped earrings in Infecting an Heir, which has some important implications for the Sentinels universe. If this matches other fantasy portrayals I've seen it means that the objects of worship themselves hold no special power. It is either faith or specific relics that are anathema to the undead, if they would work at all. Even then I don't think it would be shown to be a terribly effective means of defending yourself, after all Fanatic still has to rely on her physical sword and armor to protect her, as shown on her Prime Wardens incap (thinking we've confirmed that takes place at the Court of Blood). Even with that though, the type of dark power presented does affect Fanatic as shown in the Unhallowed Halls flavor text. Which by the way, that card makes the Court environment a heck of a lot scarier and really shuts down a few of Fanatic's and Scholar's main strategies.

 

Actually, her complete aversion to the Court's dark power, and Apostate using Blood Magic to summon his ancient relics might mean there is a connection between the two angelic beings and the vampires. With blood magic being a factor... hmmm. Could we also connect Bugbear and Atlantis' Phosphoresent Chamber back to this? Perhaps some ancient magical civilization that led to beings like the Vampires thru special rituals?

 

Madame Mittermeier's Circus.

We've got a couple of villains making an appearance here. Glamor shows up with NAturalist captured, Cueball shows up fighting Guise, we do not though get the Madame herself. I doubt it is Glamor, though I do think Glamor knows who the Madame is.

 

Maze of Mirrors in the Circus is the source of Setback and Tachyon's encounters with Glamor.It also shows Wraith a few different versions of herself. Not sure if we're talking more alternate realities or simply stage magic but Spite Wraith and Ghoul Wraith are both fairly terrifying looking.

 

Shooting Gallery is a bit of fin for side characters. It looks like we have Tachyon's wife Dana (which if Glamor is closely associated with the circus explains the nemesis icon between the two). I think the General in the middle is General Armstrong who ran Fort Adamant while Bunker was there. The third person is either Mrs. or Miss Parsons I think. My original guess was Mrs. Parsons, it fit the theme of non-super relatives and family and the cuffs looked too flimsy to hold Pauline, but then I think we see Pauline in You won't believe your eyes with "Baron Blade" (a fake, either illusion or possibly the counterfiet Blade from Biomancer). Could have the real Mrs. Parson's in danger and illusions of Pauline as "Ivanna" I guess, but all in all, I don't think it was a fun day for LEgacy or whichever villain he eventually caught up to who threatened his family.

 

Temple of Zhu Long kind of disappointed me for huge story secrets. Maybe I just missed them, but there was nothing big and obvious.

 

There is something though I think. Mysterious Ceremonies shows two women with scars over their eyes, it looks like a ritualistic blinding. The Operative also has symbolic blinding thru the red paint and later the dragon tatoo. Fixer is blind, and we've never seen his eyes. Fixer was also Zhu Long's nemesis long before Dark Watch Fixer. What if Fixer has a longer history with the Dragon, from back before he was Black Fist even, after all, someone needed to teach him martial arts.

 

 

 

Okay, whew. I'm going to post this massive post, then post two hold in spots to fill ou tomorrow because it is late and I still have 10 decks and a few meta thoughts to go through. Luckily, I'm mostly using some sheets I paper I jotted notes on while I was first going thru the cards.

posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
Okay, back, have my coffee and talking about Miss Information

 

Which in terms of new story elements... I had a thought. Her incap side got me thinking. With the straight jacket and the glowing eyes... is it possible that Miss Information is the Time-Crazed Prisoner? Time-Crazed prisoner is important to the lore, since they have given us so much info, and with her falling through realities to avoid her death and developing reality-warping powers she fits the bill. Plus FILTER is the only likely canidate to be able to hold her, since their prison is removed from reality and they have reality tech themselves according to KNYFE's bio. Pure speculation, but I think it clicks together.

 

There is also some pure speculation on the Wraith. On the card Endless Possibilities we see a Wraith covered in a lot more bandages than the normal Wraith, and it got me thinking about Wraith and her costume. Bandage wraps are an odd choice for her costume, and this alternate version feels darker, and has more bandages. What if the bandages are symbolic? Thye might reresent the extent of Maia's injuries when she was beaten by those thugs and left in a coma. Following that thread, this new version would be a version of Maia who was beaten even more severly. Not sure if we can do anything with it, but it raises some interesting ideas about the Wraith I think.

 

Ambuscade

 

Ambuscade's incap side shows us his "disfiguring scars" and suddenly I have much less respect for Ambuscade. It tells us just how crazy and narscisitic he is, but seriously, that is less than minor.

 

Interestingly, Desert Eagle from the deck seems to know about Haka's past and his banishment, which I think we'd established happened hundreds of years ago, which raises some questions. Either, since I think a lot of Maori history follows oral tradition, Haka's legends are still floating around or Desert Eagle is fairly old himself.

 

MAgman is interesting. He is clearly from Magmaria, but would have had to make his first appearance before Magmaria did. Also, why is he on the surface instead of where he belongs, and why is he obviously crazy compared to his brethren? The cards don't give any hints I can find, comic tropes would tell us being on the surface is what drove him mad but it might have some important story implications.

 

Biomancer

I think, despite the different styles of art, that we can safely say the Homunculus is the green being from Lightspeed barrage, there are enough similiarites though and we see Tachyon fighting the homunculus.

 

The use of steel skeletons brings me to question a few things. Could Biomancer be the source of the Robot Legacy we see in Tactics, or even Golem Unity? The design of the metal we see on his incap side matches. Robo-Legacy fits with Biomancers normal SOP, but Unity would be a massive prize. Her power to manipulate metal, combined with his ability to manipulate flesh would be massive.

 

BugBear

 

We see Naturalist being hunted by Bugbear, and Bugbear seems to be sucking the life out of Calypso in a different card. Both of which could be important or meaningless.

More interestingly, we see Ammit from the Tomb of Anubis make his debut as a card. His flavor text is fascinating to read, stating most likely to Ra that if he stays on the path he has chosen his form will remain bound to this plane but his spirit will fade away. I think I saw a Footenotes that I commented on where this ties into a theory about where Tactics Ra is from. I think Ra changed his path, possibly losing the Ra of old to prevent the death of the body of Washington, but thereby needing a new host for the power of Ra. It is also fascinating that Ammit is shown outside the tomb, that tells me that Ammit was sent to hunt down Ra. I think there might be more to the struggle amongst the Egyptian pantheon characters... maybe Anubis and Ammit represent a force trying to destroy the spirits that have cheated death to continue their existence for thousands of years?

 

Quetzalcoatl has a big red crystal, another possible Oblivion Shard.

 

Bugbear's incap is really interesting to me. From his bio we get the feeling that there is a human side of Bugbear that is trying to find a way to lift his cursed hunger. Nightmist is that person, but the only time we see them together she has sealed him away, and is crying and caressing his face. IS she simply distraught because she couldn't save him, or did something more develop between them?

 

Hammer and Anvil

 

I think the red beam we see on Cover Fire is from O-X, most likely before the card that shows Hammer burning him from the inside out.

 

Our biggest thing here is the Bio and Hammer's Incap side. The Bio tells us that one of the reasons Dawn sent them out was to get the Visionary and see if she could not show a future where the Citizens of the Sun ruled. Following thru  on that, they would need Visionary under their control to help make that become a reality. If that is the case, did Hammer somehow end up trying to dominate the Visionaries mind and we see the result of that. Being of course, he got beat bad. We see a firey Hammer captured by a large, green, Six armed (spider theme or Hindu reference?) Dark Visionary. We also see normal visionary, pink energy, sealed in green crystal behind Dark Visionary. Since these are pure representations of their minds, it might be giving us something towards what Dark Visionary is, what kind of world she might have been from... oooh. If it is a spider reference does that mean we should look at the Grotesque Arachnid for some more clues?

 

Greazer

 

Galactra states that Captain Cosmic's power is merely an Echo. What if she is right? If Cosmic's power is an echo of the "Cosmos" (and we know we have a Cosmic Entity coming)? Connections there could be very interesting.

 

Oh, why tangent because I missed something. Incap of Prime Wardens Captain Cosmic shows him being captured by the Celestial Adjudicator of the Tribunal. Can't believe I missed that before now. COuld he be considered a "vigilante of cosmic proportions"?

 

We also now know that the enemy we see on Wounding Buffer is Rahazar. Quite possibly an Alien, but we don't know almost anything beyond that.

 

La Capitan

It looks like Chiquito is holding O-X's head, which we also seem to see on the deck of the old La Capitan's ship as the wheel.

 

Donde? Aqui! (Where? Here! according to Google Translate) shows La Capitan working with LA Capitan. She clearly has means to communicate to herself and sems to be immune to paradoxs. Are we thinking this is all alternate reality shenanagins or simply time-wimey shenangins?

 

Temporal Kelhaul seems to be normal Mainstay's incap side, and probably hurt a lot.

 

Quando? Ahora! (Maybe supposed to be When? Now!, but google translate says When is Cuando) This card is awesome looking. We've got a huge list of alternate's. Here's what I think we've got shown:

Alternate Freedom Five with The Dreamer and her ape with a green crystal in his forehead, NAturalist as a small bird, a robotic Tachyon, possibly related to Omnitron due to coloration, and a Nightmist who might also be the Virtuoso of the Void (there is a floating set of Pan Pipes with the same mark as the Amulet of the Elder Gods and the same green energy we see with Adept). Then on the other side, a Dark Tempest (either gene-bound or related to the guy we see on the incap of prime wardens tempest) a heroic looking Plague Rat and Kismet and a guy who I think may be a Mystic MArtial Arts Setback, translation of the Kanji might reveal something but I can't provide that.

 

So... I hate time travel as a story device, it gets so confusing and La Capitan's incap makes my brain hurt. We are shown the new Capitan being left in front of the old Capitan, but we also know that the orignal Capitan still happens, so does she somehow escape from herself who should know how she escapes and then should be able to stop it or does she kill herself which I can't beleive she'd be stupid enough to try since then she wouldn't have wanted to get herself since she knew she'd kill herself.... ouch... time travel!!!

 

Plague Rat doesn't give us anything too new, but we do know Plague rat is considered Subject 18-PZ4 which might be interesting

 

Sergeant Steel

His incap seems to show Becky Blast immediately before the scarring we see her with in Tactics. Pretty sure we can confirm the explosives expert is Becky Blast anyways

 

Espionagent is very similiar to the FILTER Spy, except for some minor dfferences in the armor.

 

Operative only gives us two new character confirmations

 

Mayor Overbrook (mayor of Rook City I assume) seems to be the most likely canidate to be the yellow figure on Rook City Wraith's incap, making the list Spite, Equity, Overbrook and Ermine)

 

Idolater seems to be the guy who was the target of Brutal Censure, either before and that causes what seems to be the scar on his forehead or afterwards and it isn't a scar as I think it is

The use of steel skeletons brings me to question a few things. Could Biomancer be the source of the Robot Legacy we see in Tactics, or even Golem Unity? The design of the metal we see on his incap side matches. Robo-Legacy fits with Biomancers normal SOP, but Unity would be a massive prize. Her power to manipulate metal, combined with his ability to manipulate flesh would be massive.

 

BugBear

 

We see Naturalist being hunted by Bugbear, and Bugbear seems to be sucking the life out of Calypso in a different card. Both of which could be important or meaningless.

More interestingly, we see Ammit from the Tomb of Anubis make his debut as a card. His flavor text is fascinating to read, stating most likely to Ra that if he stays on the path he has chosen his form will remain bound to this plane but his spirit will fade away. I think I saw a Footenotes that I commented on where this ties into a theory about where Tactics Ra is from. I think Ra changed his path, possibly losing the Ra of old to prevent the death of the body of Washington, but thereby needing a new host for the power of Ra. It is also fascinating that Ammit is shown outside the tomb, that tells me that Ammit was sent to hunt down Ra. I think there might be more to the struggle amongst the Egyptian pantheon characters... maybe Anubis and Ammit represent a force trying to destroy the spirits that have cheated death to continue their existence for thousands of years?

 

Quetzalcoatl has a big red crystal, another possible Oblivion Shard.

 

Bugbear's incap is really interesting to me. From his bio we get the feeling that there is a human side of Bugbear that is trying to find a way to lift his cursed hunger. Nightmist is that person, but the only time we see them together she has sealed him away, and is crying and caressing his face. IS she simply distraught because she couldn't save him, or did something more develop between them?

 

Hammer and Anvil

 

I think the red beam we see on Cover Fire is from O-X, most likely before the card that shows Hammer burning him from the inside out.

 

Our biggest thing here is the Bio and Hammer's Incap side. The Bio tells us that one of the reasons Dawn sent them out was to get the Visionary and see if she could not show a future where the Citizens of the Sun ruled. Following thru  on that, they would need Visionary under their control to help make that become a reality. If that is the case, did Hammer somehow end up trying to dominate the Visionaries mind and we see the result of that. Being of course, he got beat bad. We see a firey Hammer captured by a large, green, Six armed (spider theme or Hindu reference?) Dark Visionary. We also see normal visionary, pink energy, sealed in green crystal behind Dark Visionary. Since these are pure representations of their minds, it might be giving us something towards what Dark Visionary is, what kind of world she might have been from... oooh. If it is a spider reference does that mean we should look at the Grotesque Arachnid for some more clues?

 

Greazer

 

Galactra states that Captain Cosmic's power is merely an Echo. What if she is right? If Cosmic's power is an echo of the "Cosmos" (and we know we have a Cosmic Entity coming)? Connections there could be very interesting.

 

Oh, why tangent because I missed something. Incap of Prime Wardens Captain Cosmic shows him being captured by the Celestial Adjudicator of the Tribunal. Can't believe I missed that before now. COuld he be considered a "vigilante of cosmic proportions"?

 

We also now know that the enemy we see on Wounding Buffer is Rahazar. Quite possibly an Alien, but we don't know almost anything beyond that.

 

La Capitan

It looks like Chiquito is holding O-X's head, which we also seem to see on the deck of the old La Capitan's ship as the wheel.

 

Donde? Aqui! (Where? Here! according to Google Translate) shows La Capitan working with LA Capitan. She clearly has means to communicate to herself and sems to be immune to paradoxs. Are we thinking this is all alternate reality shenanagins or simply time-wimey shenangins?

 

Temporal Kelhaul seems to be normal Mainstay's incap side, and probably hurt a lot.

 

Quando? Ahora! (Maybe supposed to be When? Now!, but google translate says When is Cuando) This card is awesome looking. We've got a huge list of alternate's. Here's what I think we've got shown:

Alternate Freedom Five with The Dreamer and her ape with a green crystal in his forehead, NAturalist as a small bird, a robotic Tachyon, possibly related to Omnitron due to coloration, and a Nightmist who might also be the Virtuoso of the Void (there is a floating set of Pan Pipes with the same mark as the Amulet of the Elder Gods and the same green energy we see with Adept). Then on the other side, a Dark Tempest (either gene-bound or related to the guy we see on the incap of prime wardens tempest) a heroic looking Plague Rat and Kismet and a guy who I think may be a Mystic MArtial Arts Setback, translation of the Kanji might reveal something but I can't provide that.

 

So... I hate time travel as a story device, it gets so confusing and La Capitan's incap makes my brain hurt. We are shown the new Capitan being left in front of the old Capitan, but we also know that the orignal Capitan still happens, so does she somehow escape from herself who should know how she escapes and then should be able to stop it or does she kill herself which I can't beleive she'd be stupid enough to try since then she wouldn't have wanted to get herself since she knew she'd kill herself.... ouch... time travel!!!

 

Plague Rat doesn't give us anything too new, but we do know Plague rat is considered Subject 18-PZ4 which might be interesting

 

Sergeant Steel

His incap seems to show Becky Blast immediately before the scarring we see her with in Tactics. Pretty sure we can confirm the explosives expert is Becky Blast anyways

 

Espionagent is very similiar to the FILTER Spy, except for some minor dfferences in the armor.

 

Operative only gives us two new character confirmations

 

Mayor Overbrook (mayor of Rook City I assume) seems to be the most likely canidate to be the yellow figure on Rook City Wraith's incap, making the list Spite, Equity, Overbrook and Ermine)

 

Idolater seems to be the guy who was the target of Brutal Censure, either before and that causes what seems to be the scar on his forehead or afterwards and it isn't a scar as I think it is

posts.cooked:
And now onto some misc and interesting things.

 

First off, Magmaria's Smoldering Crystal and the circus' Wheel of Misfortune both have flavor text showing moments between Expat and Setback which I think is kind of sweet to help build up a bit of their relationship

 

Also, a lot of cards started showing Scholar of the Inifinite and Guise together. Scholar's incap, Celestial Tribunal's Paragon of Sentience, La Capitan's Donde? Aqui!, these two obviously started working together a lot which might have some major signifigance.

 

Another really important thing to pay attention to is what we don't see. And what we don;t see anywhere is the Aeon Men. Well, not entirely accurate but seeing the Scholar and Guise fighting them in Paragon of Sentience isn't what I mean. This tells me that the Aeon men are defintely part of the final expansion, and maybe even the final battle. After all, here's all the instances of seeing them I can remember:

 

Paragon of Sentience: Scholar and Guise fighting a large group of Aeon Men

Syncopated Onslaught: Argent Adept fighting a group of Aeon Men

Thorathian Monolith: Sky-Scraper fighting a large group of Aeon Men

Incidental Contact: KNYFE fighting a group of Aeon Men

Defensive Blast: O-X fighting a large group of Aeon Men

 

With all of these looking to be at different times and places... I wonder if the Aeon Men represent a massive invasion, even bigger than the Thorathian invasion from Voss. That could be a hint towards what the final fight will be like

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
Finally I can talk about stuff!!!! Ok. Where to start.....

  • Writhe was talked about a bit in this thread. I had a theory about Writhe from the moment we saw him in the V5 expansion which you can read here. It seems that I was pretty spot on, at least the new artwork supports my view more than refutes it. The Spiderman-Setback/Writhe-Venom correlation is so strong in the artwork. Look out for the "Cloak" to be a possible villain candidate moving forward.
  • I think it will be no surprise that one of the most facinating loose storylines coming out of the new artwork pertains to Scholar and Guise. Scholar's promo incap suggests to me a strong connection between them since they are both fading/melting away together at the same time. This combined with a non-trivial amount of other artwork showing them together really ticks my interest meter. I'm sure the connection between them lays within "ley-lines". Guise is the opposite coin face of Wager Master, who himself maybe the opposite coin face of our big bad cosmic entity. With Scholar and his stone being a possible "gateway"  between our world and the cosmic entity (as hinted at in his bio), there is more at play here than we know. This is a hero pairing to keep a close eye on in the final expansion.
  • Let's talk about Ammit!

If this is the path you choose, your form will be bound to this plane, but your spirit will fade

-Ammit, Ra: Horus of Two Horizons

The innitial thought here is that Ammit is more than likely talking to Ra right? There seems to be some sort of deal being made where Ra would get more powerful in order to go back and defeat the Ennead at the cost of his spirit. Given the comic this comes from, it makes a ton of sense as something thats possible. Given the backstory to "beard Ra", this would neatly explain his long absence as well as his more powered-up glorious return to kick some major egyptian ass. This looks pretty cut-and-dry here.

But I'd like to pose an alternate theory. What if he is not talking to Ra, but to Nightmist instead? Consider the following:

  • Form bound to a plane without a spirit. That could be said of Ra, as going forward in Tactics, we see the form of Ra but as a different person for all accounts. But we see the same thing with Nightmist in Tactics as well. Her mistform is bound to this plane, but she as a person/consiousness is no where to be found and considered lost/dead.
  • In the Tomb of Anubis deck, The Staff of Anubis has flavor texts suggesting that she has weilded the staff and felt its power. It's a strong connection to Ra's story and to the Underworld where Ammit is from. 
  • It has not been talked about too much, but Dark Watch Nightmist clearly has Egyptian infuences with the markings under her eyes. Nothing about it is in her backstory, but the art decision is likely not arbitrary. 
  •  Ammit is marked as a nemesis to Ra. A nemesis. Why would there be a deal here, why would Ammit allow a nemesis some support even if it comes as a sizable cost? It's possible sure, but the interaction doesn't sound as one between enemies. Another possible point for this conversation being with someone other than Ra? This is a far weaker point than the others, but it's somethign I thought worth considering.

A lot of this depends on timing, and we don't know 100% when the Horus storyline takes place in the grand scheme of things. We also know that Ra is also saved by Fanatic at some point in the "Trial by Fire" one-shot comic, but again, when that takes place exactly is nearly impossible to tell (though from the art I would guess Fanatic saves him post bearded transformation). Is it possible that Nightmist has a significant hand in Ra's ascention to Horus, going so far as to give up her spirit to save/help Ra? 

  • How cool is the card Quando? Ahora! ?!?! Not really much to say here that hasn't been said. But the brief look into an alternate universe and far different story paths for familiar heros/villains is pretty fugg'in cool.
  • How cool is Hammer/Anvil's incap art?! We knew from bio's that Dark Visionary went well past the acceptable line when dealing with the villains she fought, and this seems to be a picture of just that. With our Vanessas concious trapped in the background, I wouldn't be surprised if we see more art related to the "purging of Dark Visionary" in the future (or at least I hope to see it!)
  • As my final note, I think there is more than enough evidence to back up the theory that Heartbreaker is Tony Torus that BraithWhite posed a long while ago. The more we see of him, the more signs point to this being correct.

But the brief look into an alternate universe and far different story paths for familiar heros/villains is pretty fugg'in cool.How cool is Hammer/Anvil's incap art?! We knew from bio's that Dark Visionary went well past the acceptable line when dealing with the villains she fought, and this seems to be a picture of just that. With our Vanessas concious trapped in the background, I wouldn't be surprised if we see more art related to the "purging of Dark Visionary" in the future (or at least I hope to see it!)As my final note, I think there is more than enough evidence to back up the theory that Heartbreaker is Tony Torus that BraithWhite posed a long while ago. The more we see of him, the more signs point to this being correct.

 

I hadn't considered the flip between Guise and Wager Master, that makes Paragon of Sentience even more important if we can draw a strong connection between Scholar and the Cosmic Entity.

 

On Ammit and Nightmist… I don't know if I agree that Mist Storm is Nightmist. It never seemed a terribly compelling arguement to me, and now that we have Darkwatch Nightmist's bio I think her story might be seperate. Darkwatch Nightmist is an Eldritch being of Magic, when she was human she got trapped in a different dimension and did the whole "10,000 years in a blink of an eye" struggle to get back to Earth and not fall prey to other powerful magical spirits. Sure in that way that she "is the Mists" now it could make sense, but only if she completely lost control, which after what she went thru seems very unlikely.

 

However, I think I have another answer to why she is not in Tactics yet (I feel good saying she will be in it at some point). Bugbear's incap seems to show a connection between Nightmist and Bugbear, and his story seems to hint that he sought her out for help curing him. She wasn't able to, and couldn't devote time to saving him with the world falling apart around their ears with Progeny and whatever comes afterward. What if after the final battle she devotes herself to study to find a cure? Or, perhaps working on strengthening Earth's mystical defenses (in case Scholar and Guise goes down and leylines crumble). If she has secluded herself and is working solo on something only she can do (or that she thinks she can only do since Faye seems to have that sort of lone ranger mentality) then it makes since she is no longer with Dark Watch, who is more concerned with helping take care of Broken City. Actually, Nightmist might have moved on from Mystic Detective to Sorcerer Supreme and instead works more closely with the Prime Wardens (many of whom are conspicously absent and might be a clue that something else big is still going on in the world that is requiring their attention).

 

Also supporting Heartbreaker is Tony Taurus, especially since the Tribunal shows that Heartbreaker is most likely responsible for the death of Tremata, if Tremata (an ally in Rook City) is dead, then we have to wonder what happens to the other doomed ally, and man does Tony and Heartbreaker seem to fit so well together
